Name: Jeronimos Monastery
Cost Range: 18 EUR adult, ~9 EUR youth 13-24 with ID, under 12 free; church free
Tips: BOOKED AND PAID - cloister Tue 25 Aug 2026 at 15:30, order 38185413 (moved off Day 1 - the voucher had no Sunday slot). Free church done Day 1 at 14:00. Bring photo ID for the two youth tickets. Closed Mondays. Portugals greatest Manueline building (1501). Tombs of Vasco da Gama and Luis de Camoes. The free church never needs a ticket — but keeps Sunday hours 14:00-17:00 (Mass mornings).
Family: Excellent — stunning for all ages book ahead

Name: Belem Tower
Cost Range: 15 EUR adult, 7.50 EUR youth 13-24 with ID, under 12 free
Tips: BOOKED - order 38185394, paid, Aug 23 16:00 slot — at the gate 15:55. Reopened 26 May 2026 after a 13-month 1M-euro restoration; all four levels + terrace open again with strict timed entry (60 people per 30 min, 900/day). Closed Mondays. Find the rhinoceros on the north bastion.
Family: Good — multiple levels narrow stairs best for ages 5+

Name: Monument to the Discoveries
Cost Range: 10 EUR adult, under 12 free; youth rate — ask at desk
Tips: 52m white stone prow-shaped monument (1960). 33 historical figures led by Henry the Navigator. Take the lift to the top for the best single view in Belem. Giant world map mosaic on the pavement is best seen from above. Daily 10:00-19:00 Mar-Sep.

Name: Sao Jorge Castle
Address: Rua de Santa Cruz do Castelo 1100-129 Lisboa
Cost Range: 17 EUR adult, 8.50 EUR youth 13-25 with ID, under 12 free
Tips: BOOKED - paid, open ticket valid until 1 Nov 2026, entry from 09:00. Daily 09:00-21:00 summer. Moorish-era hilltop fortress with 360 degree panoramas. Walkable ramparts towers archaeological site. Peacocks roam freely. Camera Obscura in Torre de Ulisses is magical. Go at 09:00 opening (our Day 3).
Family: Excellent — peacocks ramparts archaeology all engage kids

Name: Carmo Convent
Cost Range: 7 EUR adult, under 14 free, 5 EUR with student ID
Tips: Hauntingly beautiful Gothic convent whose roof was destroyed in the 1755 earthquake and never rebuilt — Gothic arches now frame open sky. Inside: small museum with Egyptian mummies Pre-Columbian artefacts and medieval stonework. Mon-Sat 10:00-19:00 May-Oct, closed Sundays (our Day 4 is a Wednesday). Allow 45-60 mins.
Family: Good — mummies and open-sky arches engage all ages

Name: Oceanario de Lisboa
Address: Esplanada D Carlos I Parque das Nacoes 1990-005 Lisboa
Cost Range: Time-banded 2026: 29 EUR morning / 27 EUR 12:00-15:30 / 25 EUR from 16:00; ages 13+ pay adult; child 3-12 15-18 EUR
Tips: One of Europes finest aquariums. Single massive central ocean tank with sharks sea otters and a rare sunfish. Book the 12:00 band for our Day 4 (Wed Aug 26) — timed entry sells out in August. Daily 10:00-20:00 last entry 19:00. Allow 2 hrs. Lockers max 47.5x30x46cm — no suitcases, leave bags at the apartment.
Family: Outstanding — sea otters and shark tunnel are unmissable

Name: MAAT Museum of Art Architecture Technology
Cost Range: 11 EUR galleries, under 12 free, free 1st Sun morning; rooftop walkway free to everyone
Tips: Architecturally striking curved building by Amanda Levete beside the Tagus. The rooftop walkway is free to everyone — one of Lisbons best vantage points, on the Day 1 walk back from Belem Tower. Galleries closed Tuesdays.
Family: Good — free rooftop is the draw even without museum entry

Name: Museu do Azulejo
Address: Rua da Madre de Deus 4 1900-312 Lisboa
Tips: The only museum in the world dedicated to azulejo. 36-metre panoramic tile panel depicting pre-earthquake Lisbon (c.1738). Housed in a stunning 16th-century convent. Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00 closed Mon. Carried a temporarily-closed flag in mid-2026 listings — verify before going. Not in this trips plan.

Name: Se Cathedral
Cost Range: 5 EUR (includes treasury), kids 7-12 3 EUR; free for Mass-goers
Tips: Lisbons oldest church (1147). Now ticketed — and the Gothic cloister with the Roman garum excavation is CLOSED for long-term works, so the best bit is off the menu. Optional quick visit on the Day 3 descent. Mon-Sat ~09:30-18:30, closed Sundays to visitors.
Family: Good — quick visit while the cloister works run

Name: LX Factory
Tips: 19th-century industrial complex — independent shops studios street food vintage market. Sunday market Feira da LX (noon-7pm). On this trip its the Day 4 fallback morning (Wednesday = regular shops, no market). Free entry always.
Family: Excellent — Sunday market is the highlight for families

Name: Praca do Comercio
Tips: One of Europes largest squares stretching along the Tagus. The Arco da Rua Augusta offers panoramic views. Best at sunset (~20:20 during our stay) — Day 1 evening is timed to it.
Family: Excellent — free flat easy to walk

Name: Rossio Square
Tips: Historic heart of Baixa. Distinctive wave-patterned black-and-white cobblestone pavement. Baroque fountains neoclassical theatre. Stop for ginjinha (1.50 EUR) at the traditional bars on the edge. Pickpocket-aware here.

Name: Parque das Nacoes
Cost Range: Free to enter individual attractions vary
Tips: Modern district built for Expo 98. Santiago Calatravas Oriente station Alvaro Sizas Portugal Pavilion cable car over the Tagus. Our Day 4 midday zone — Oriente is 3 Metro stops from the airport, which the departure plan exploits.

Name: Elevador de Santa Justa
Tips: CLOSED for maintenance as of 2026 — do not queue or pay. Neo-Gothic cast-iron lift (1902) connecting Baixa to Chiado. Best free view of the ironwork and deck is from the Largo do Carmo side (Day 4 morning).
Family: N/A while closed — view from Carmo side

Name: Museu Calouste Gulbenkian
Cost Range: 14 EUR free Sun after 2pm under 18 free
Tips: Finest private art collection assembled by one person — 6000 pieces: Egyptian Islamic Rembrandt Rubens Turner Lalique and Impressionists. Wed-Mon 10:00-18:00 closed Tue. Carried a temporarily-closed flag in mid-2026 — verify if visiting. Free garden retreat from city heat. Not in this trips plan.

Name: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga
Tips: Portugals most important art museum. The Polyptych of St Vincent by Nuno Goncalves (~1470) is a defining work of Portuguese art. Garden terrace has some of the best Tagus views in Lisbon. Tue 2pm-6pm is quietest. Closed Mon.

Name: Museu do Fado
Address: Largo do Chafariz de Dentro 1 1100-139 Lisboa (Alfama)
Tips: Richly designed museum dedicated to Fado. Audio stations legendary recordings instrument exhibits. Put on headphones and listen to Amalia Rodrigues in full. Our Day 3 Option B (air-conditioned) — the primer for that nights fado dinner at Parreirinha. Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00 closed Mon.

Name: Pavilhao do Conhecimento
Tips: Exceptional hands-on science museum in Parque das Nacoes. Curious kids 5-14 can spend hours here. Only fits our Day 4 if the Oceanario slot grows into a full half-day — unlikely on departure day.

Name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
Address: Rua da Senhora do Monte Graca 1170 Lisboa
Tips: The highest miradouro in Lisbon with almost 360 degree panorama. Somehow less crowded than Graca or Santa Luzia despite best overall view. Sunday afternoons locals bring wine and guitars. Our Day 3 no-fado sunset alternative (~20:19).

Name: Miradouro da Graca
Tips: Wide 160 degree panorama shaded by stone pines. Esplanada da Graca kiosk serves cold beers since 1992. Castle silhouette at dusk is spectacular.

Name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
Address: Largo de Santa Luzia Alfama 1100 Lisboa
Tips: Terrace behind the Igreja de Santa Luzia draped in roses under grapevine pergolas. Two large azulejo tile panels depict pre-1755 Lisbon. More intimate than Portas do Sol. On our Day 3 route ~10:45.

Name: Miradouro das Portas do Sol
Address: Largo das Portas do Sol Alfama 1100 Lisboa
Tips: Sweeping view over Alfama rooftops to Tagus and National Pantheon. One of Lisbons most photographed spots. Go before the cruise-ship crowds — Day 3 hits it right after the castle.

Name: Miradouro de Sao Pedro de Alcantara
Address: Rua de Sao Pedro de Alcantara Bairro Alto 1200 Lisboa
Tips: Large terraced garden in Bairro Alto. Faces east across Baixa to the castle. Night view when castle is lit is stunning — our Day 1 nightcap. Gloria funicular alongside is closed; walk up (5 min steep).

Name: Miradouro de Santa Catarina Adamastor
Address: Rua de Santa Catarina Bica/Chiado 1200 Lisboa
Tips: Bohemian terrace with stone Adamastor monster sculpture. Popular with students and musicians. Faces west for best 25 de Abril bridge sunset light.

Name: Jardim do Torel
Tips: A hilltop garden that feels like an oasis — unknown even to many Lisboetas. High above Avenida da Liberdade with sweeping views south to the Tagus. Kiosk cafe in the shade. 15 min from our apartment.

Name: Tapada das Necessidades
Tips: Former royal garden — 10 hectares one of the largest green spaces in central Lisbon yet almost entirely tourist-free. Three ornamental lakes Europes oldest cactus collection peacocks and exotic trees.

Name: Estufa Fria
Address: Parque Eduardo VII Av Alvares Cabral 1070 Lisboa
Tips: Tucked into Parque Eduardo VII — 300+ plant species beneath a slatted-wood canopy. Small waterfalls hidden caves koi ponds in three interconnected glasshouses. Free Sundays until 14:00.
Family: Excellent — the enclosed glasshouses with waterfalls delight kids

Name: Casa do Alentejo
Address: Rua das Portas de Santo Antao 58 1150-268 Lisboa
Tips: Behind an unmarked door near Rossio hides a 17th-century palace with a jaw-dropping Moorish courtyard azulejo-lined walls and ornate wooden ceilings. Walk past the restaurant into the side rooms stairwells and courtyard — free to explore.
Family: Good — the surprise factor is the draw

Name: Museu Bordalo Pinheiro Garden
Cost Range: Garden free; museum has entry fee
Tips: Dedicated to Portugals great satirical ceramicist. The adjoining garden has giant porcelain frogs crabs lobsters and snakes lurking among trees. Garden is free — no ticket needed. Walk it first then tour the museum.
Family: Excellent — the giant ceramic creatures are hilarious and memorable for kids

Name: Hospital de Bonecas
Tips: Operating since 1830 from its original townhouse. One of the worlds oldest doll repair shops — part curiosity cabinet part museum with 3500+ dolls. Ask to see the repair workshop. Kids love it or find it unsettling.

Name: Museu do Oriente
Address: Av Brasilia Doca de Alcantara Norte 1350-302 Lisboa
Tips: Under-visited powerhouse in an Alcantara waterfront warehouse. Portugals connections to Asia from the Age of Discovery. Gods of Asia floor from the Kwok On collection is extraordinary. Free Friday evenings.

Name: Museu da Agua Reservatorio Mae d Agua das Amoreiras
Tips: Cavernous underground cistern (1746) holding 5500 cubic metres of water beneath soaring vaulted arches. Currently hosts immersive art projections. Acoustics and scale are remarkable. Panoramic terrace above for rooftop views.

Name: Mouraria — Rua do Capelao Tile Murals
Tips: True heart of Mouraria and birthplace of Fado. Rua do Capelao is covered in tile artwork honouring local fado singers. Beco das Farinhas has striking photographic portraits of elderly residents. Wander without a map.

Name: Largo do Intendente
Address: Largo do Intendente Pina Manique 1100-285 Lisboa
Tips: Creative heart of Mourarias north side — azulejo-clad square multicultural hub of artists freelancers and local families. Great for an authentic warm evening in a square that feels nothing like a tourist bar. 10 min from our apartment.

Name: Prazeres Cemetery
Address: Estrada de Sao Domingos de Benfica 1350-297 Lisboa
Tips: Lisbons grand Victorian necropolis (1833). 12 hectares with 82 numbered streets of extraordinary funerary architecture azulejo tombs Gothic chapels. Views over the Tagus and 25 de Abril bridge. Day 3 Option A finale via tram 28/25. Daily ~09:00-18:00.
Family: Good for those who love church and cemetery architecture — the Gothic Revival chapels are outstanding

Name: Feira da Ladra
Address: Campo de Santa Clara Graca Lisboa (Tue and Sat mornings)
Tips: Lisbons famous outdoor flea market — Tuesdays and Saturdays only, and our Day 3 is a Tuesday, right beside Sao Vicente. Mix of genuine antiques old azulejo tiles vintage goods. Great for vintage tile souvenirs. Bags zipped.

Name: Alfama District
Address: Centred on Largo do Chafariz de Dentro 1100 Lisboa
Tips: Lisbons oldest district — Moorish labyrinth of whitewashed houses steep cobbled alleys and laundry-draped windows. Birthplace of Fado. Day 3 walks it top-to-bottom (castle to Se). Wander before 10am for a completely different experience from the tourist-crowded midday.
Family: Good — cobblestones challenging for very young children; magical for all ages

Name: Mouraria
Address: Centred on Largo do Intendente Lisboa
Tips: Lisbons most multicultural quarter. True birthplace of Fado. More authentic and less polished than Alfama. Cheaper and more diverse food scene.

Name: Principe Real
Tips: Lisbons most refined neighbourhood. Wide tree-lined boulevards antique shops concept stores Saturday farmers and antique market in the central garden. Day 4 fallback morning option.

Name: LX Factory area / Alcantara
Tips: Former 19th-century industrial complex under the 25 de Abril bridge. Sunday Feira da LX market (noon-7pm). Artisani gelato branch at nearby Doca de Santo Amaro.
Family: Excellent on Sundays for the market

Name: Marvila Creative District
Address: Praca David Leandro da Silva 8 1950 Lisboa
Tips: Lisbons Brooklyn. Former wine warehouses now hosting craft breweries street art galleries design studios. 8 Marvila (2024) is a 22000 sqm covered creative village. Still largely a local secret.

Name: Belem
Cost Range: Free to walk — individual monuments vary
Tips: Grand wide-boulevarded district 6km west of centre. Portugals greatest Age of Discovery monuments. More spacious than central Lisbon. Our Day 1 stage — flat, easy, everything within 10 min on foot.
Family: Excellent — most family-friendly major neighbourhood in Lisbon

Name: Tram 28E
Cost Range: 3.20 EUR single on board (1.90 with Viva card)
Tips: Iconic vintage yellow tram 38 stops through Alfama Chiado and Estrela. Heavily targeted by pickpockets 9am-6pm in August. Board at Prazeres quiet western end to avoid queuing. Early morning or after 6pm to avoid worst crowds — or walk the Alfama stretch as Day 3 does.

Name: Tram 24
Address: Praca Luis de Camoes to Campolide
Cost Range: 3.20 EUR single on board (1.90 with Viva card)
Tips: Quiet route using historic yellow trams through Chiado and Principe Real. Far less crowded than Tram 28 but equally photogenic. Locally recommended as the better alternative.

Name: Sintra — Pena Palace
Cost Range: 20 EUR adult (Essential Visit); reduced youth band — check at purchase
Tips: BOOKED & paid — Essential Visit, 20 EUR adult, 09:00 palace slot for Mon Aug 24. The 09:00 is the PALACE door, 15-25 min uphill from the park gate — taxi/Bolt up from Sintra station (~10-15 EUR total), the first 434 bus is too late. Enter within ~30 min of slot or forfeit.
Family: Outstanding for all ages — book ahead essential

Name: Sintra — Quinta da Regaleira
Cost Range: 20 EUR adult, 15 EUR youth 6-17, free under 6, family 2+2 pack 60 EUR (2026 prices)
Tips: BOOKED & PAID - Mon Aug 24, entry window 14:30-15:00, MEO Blueticket 38339594, 80.54 EUR for our four (Emily at 18 pays adult). Download the ticket PDFs; the email is not a ticket. Eccentric neo-Manueline estate (1910): the Initiation Well, a 27-metre spiral staircase into underground tunnels. Bring a small torch.
Family: Outstanding — the underground tunnels are extraordinary for families

Name: Sintra — National Palace of Sintra
Tips: Only palace in the actual village centre. Two enormous cone-shaped chimneys are Sintra's defining symbol. Sala dos Brasoes (Hall of Crests) and Sala dos Cisnes (Swan Hall) are highlights. Walk-in. Not in our day plan — the chimneys get admired from the lunch table.

Name: Sintra — Moorish Castle
Cost Range: 12 EUR adult, reduced youth band; on-site ticket booth CLOSED — buy at Pena's ticket office
Tips: 8th-9th century Moorish hilltop fortification 10 min from Pena's gate. Dramatic ramparts and towers. Views over Sintra and the Atlantic from battlements. The shaded forest path down to the village (~25 min) is the day's best walk.
Family: Good — physically demanding but rewarding for kids who like climbing

Name: Sintra — Monserrate Palace
Tips: Romantic neo-Gothic/Moorish/Hindu fusion palace (1858) in beautiful botanical gardens. Less visited than Pena — good choice to avoid peak crowds. Filed for a future quieter visit.

Name: Cascais
Cost Range: Train from Cais do Sodre 2.30 EUR per person each way; bus 1624 from Cabo da Roca 2.60 EUR
Tips: Elegant coastal resort 33km west of Lisbon. Flat walkable beaches marina historic centre fish restaurants. Boca do Inferno natural rock arch is a short walk from town. NOT on this trip - the Day 2 coastal leg was cut to keep Sintra a single relaxed day. Kept as reference for a future visit.

Name: Arrabida Natural Park
Cost Range: Guided tour 50-70 EUR per person or car hire + shuttle
Tips: Turquoise coves and pine-covered limestone hills 45km south of Lisbon. Best water clarity near Lisbon. Summer car ban in effect Jun 15-Sep 15. Praia dos Galapinhos is calm shallow and safe for young children. Guided tour handles logistics. Future-trip file.
Family: Outstanding for families with young children — calm shallow water

Name: Obidos
Cost Range: Bus 7 EUR per person town entry free
Tips: Perfectly preserved medieval walled town 80km north of Lisbon. Fairytale feel reads as genuinely magical to children. Note: wall parapets have NO guardrails — supervise young children carefully. Try ginjinha in a chocolate cup. Future-trip file.
Family: Great fairy-tale feel — supervise closely on walls

Name: Sesimbra
Tips: Picturesque fishing village with sheltered calm beach in a natural bay. Considerably less crowded than Cascais. Excellent grilled fish. Moorish castle above the village. Future-trip file.
Family: Excellent — calm sheltered shallow bay perfect for young children

Name: Igreja de Sao Roque
Tips: Plain 16th-century Jesuit facade hides one of Europe's most jaw-dropping interiors — eight gilded chapels culminating in the Chapel of St John the Baptist. Built in Rome shipped to Lisbon in pieces in 1742 — the most expensive 18th-century commission in Europe. Ceiling is flat-painted trompe l oeil. Closed Mondays — our Day 3 (Tuesday) Option A anchor.
Family: Excellent for all ages — the surprise factor is extraordinary

Name: Livraria Bertrand
Tips: The oldest operating bookshop in the world (1732 Guinness certified). Labyrinth of interconnected rooms in Chiado. Poets and writers who visited include Camoes Eca de Queiros and Fernando Pessoa. Buy any book and ask for the oldest-bookshop stamp on the flyleaf.

Name: Museu Nacional dos Coches (Coach Museum)
Cost Range: ~15 EUR adult; reductions at the till
Tips: One of the world finest collections of historical royal carriages — 70+ coaches from the 17th-19th centuries. The gilded Baroque excess rivals Versailles. Pritzker Prize building. Right in the Belem cluster — our Day 1 wet-weather fallback. Closed Mon. Allow 45-60 min.
Family: Good — the gilded carriages are visually stunning for all ages

Name: Cervejaria Trindade
Tips: Portugal's oldest beer hall (1836) occupying the vaulted refectory of the 13th-century Convento da Trindade. Extraordinary azulejo panels (Science Agriculture Industry Commerce) line the soaring walls. Order a cold Sagres in the Gothic-vaulted hall and look at the tile art.
Family: Good — the architectural contrast of Gothic monastic architecture and lively brasserie is extraordinary

Name: Cacilhas Ferry and Ponto Final
Address: Ferry: Estacao Fluvial do Cais do Sodre. Restaurant: Rua do Ginjal 72 Cacilhas
Tips: Best Lisbon skyline view in the city — the 10-min Cacilhas ferry at sunset gives you the definitive panorama that no viewpoint on the city side can match. Ponto Final restaurant has tables at the river's edge. Book a riverside table. Filed for a return trip — no evening slot fits this stay.
Family: Excellent — the sunset ferry crossing is unforgettable

Name: Palacio Fronteira (Fronteira Palace)
Address: Largo de Sao Domingos de Benfica 1 1500-554 Lisboa
Tips: 17th-century palace with the finest original azulejo tile garden in Portugal. Tiles depicting Restoration War battles reflected in a rectangular tank. Still privately owned by the Marquis of Fronteira family. Guided tours Tue-Sat mornings (10:30 11:00 11:30) — reserve. Future-trip file.
Family: Good for ages 8+ who appreciate history and art

Name: Amoreiras 360
Address: Amoreiras Shopping Center tower Av Eng Duarte Pacheco 1070 Lisboa
Tips: Modern 360 degree rooftop platform on Amoreiras shopping towers — a different perspective from Lisbons historic hilltop miradouros. Glass barriers calm atmosphere telescope viewing stations. Less crowded than the famous viewpoints. Good combined with the Museu da Agua Reservatorio in the same area.

Name: Sintra — Convent of the Capuchos
Cost Range: 7 EUR adult, free under 12, approx 22 EUR for family of 4
Tips: The most eerie and extraordinary hidden place in Sintra. Tiny 16th-century Franciscan hermitage where 12 monks lined every room doorway and corridor with cork for insulation. Doorways built small so monks had to bow. Byron called it the most beautiful desolation. Almost always empty even in August — needs a taxi. Future-trip file.
Family: Outstanding — the cork cells and forest setting are unlike anything else in Portugal

Name: Cabo da Roca
Cost Range: Bus 1624 (ex-403) 2.60 EUR per person on board; optional certificate 11 EUR
Tips: The westernmost point of continental Europe — dramatic 140m cliffs plunging into the Atlantic with a lighthouse and a stone marker bearing Camoes words where land ends and sea begins. Our Day 2 late-afternoon stop via bus 1624 from Sintra (roughly hourly — check the Carris Metropolitana app). Windy and cold even in August — bring layers.
Family: Excellent — the sense of standing at the edge of Europe is genuinely powerful

Name: Sao Vicente de Fora
Address: Largo de Sao Vicente Alfama 1100-572 Lisboa
Cost Range: 8 EUR adult, 4 EUR under 25, under 12 free
Tips: BOOKED — ref 980497008 (2 adult, 2 youth) for our Day 3. Open DAILY 10:00-19:00 summer, last admission 18:00. Vast white monastery (1582). Walls lined floor-to-ceiling with azulejo panels incl. the fables set. Royal Pantheon of the Braganca dynasty. Rooftop terrace over Alfama. Feira da Ladra flea market outside Tue and Sat.

Name: Panteao Nacional (Santa Engracia)
Address: Campo de Santa Clara Alfama 1100-471 Lisboa
Cost Range: 10 EUR adult (2026 price), 5 EUR youth 13-24, under 12 free; ask about the 50% family rate
Tips: Great baroque dome begun 1682 — finished 1966, hence the phrase obras de Santa Engracia for a never-ending job. Tombs and cenotaphs of Portuguese greats including fado legend Amalia Rodrigues. Climb to the dome terrace for a 360 view. Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00 (last 17:40), closed Mondays. Day 3 stop at 12:30.

Name: MUDE
Tips: Reopened 2024 in a handsome Rua Augusta building. 2,500+ pieces spanning furniture, industrial design, and fashion from 1930s-today. Visit Sunday 10am-2pm for free entry and quietest crowds.
Family: Good — better for older kids/teens with design interest

Name: Time Out Market
Address: Av. 24 de Julho 49, 1200-479 Lisboa (Cais do Sodre)
Tips: Vast renovated 19th-century iron market hall housing 26 restaurants curated from Lisbon's top chefs. Our Day 1 dinner. Sun-Wed 10:00-24:00, Thu-Sat 10:00-02:00. Must-orders: grilled octopus, bifanas, pasteis de nata, green wine.
Family: Excellent — everyone picks their own dish

Name: Elevador da Bica
Address: Rua de Sao Paulo / Rua do Loreto, Lisboa
Tips: Most photogenic funicular, running down narrow Rua da Bica with framed Tagus views. Suspended since the Sep 2025 Gloria accident — still not running as of Aug 2026. The street itself is still the photo: walk it.

Name: Elevador do Lavra
Address: Largo da Anunciada / Rua Camara Pestana, Lisboa
Tips: Lisbon's oldest funicular (1884), steepest at 23% incline, and least-known. Suspended since Sep 2025; still not running as of Aug 2026. Jardim do Torel above is reachable on foot.

Name: Elevador da Gloria
Address: Praca dos Restauradores / Bairro Alto, Lisboa
Tips: Most famous funicular, connecting Restauradores to Sao Pedro de Alcantara viewpoint. Closed since the fatal derailment of 3 Sep 2025 and now being rebuilt. Walk the steep parallel street on foot instead — still worth it for the viewpoint.

Name: Setubal
Tips: Port city and base for Arrabida. Good fish market, Museu de Arqueologia e Etnografia (Azulejo Museum), and the Convento de Jesus (first Manueline building in Portugal). Mainly useful as an Arrabida gateway.
Family: Fine as a brief stop en route to Arrabida

Name: Evora
Tips: UNESCO-listed city in the Alentejo, 130km from Lisbon. Roman temple, medieval cathedral, medieval walls, and the Chapel of Bones. Best deferred to a separate visit — 3-hour round-trip transit and 35C+ August heat makes this a grind with young children.
Family: Better suited to older kids/adults given heat and distance

Name: Sintra — Palacio Biester
Cost Range: ~12 EUR; not currently in the day plan
Tips: Late-19th-century romantic villa by architect Jose Luiz Monteiro with an English-style botanical park. Off the main Pena/Regaleira circuit and much less crowded. A quieter alternative worth knowing for a return trip, not an addition to an already-full Sintra day.
Family: Good for ages 8+ who appreciate quieter, less-crowded architecture

Name: Sintra Mitos e Lendas
Tips: Interactive myths-and-legends centre inside the Sintra tourist office — 17 themed multimedia rooms on local legends, audio guide in 5 languages. Daily 10:00-18:30, last entry 17:30. An air-conditioned, low-effort add-on right by the Piriquita lunch stop — the swap-in if Castelo dos Mouros gets cut.
Family: Excellent — cool, easy, and good for kids around the lunch stop

Name: Igreja de Santo Antonio
Address: Largo de Santo Antonio da Se, 1100-499 Lisboa
Tips: Built over the birthplace of St Anthony of Padua — tiny, free, right beside the Se. The 5-minute add-on as you pass on the Day 3 Alfama descent.

Name: Igreja de Sao Domingos
Tips: Fire-scarred nave left raw after the 1959 blaze — haunting and unforgettable. Steps from the A Ginjinha counter; pair the two in ten minutes any evening.

Name: Miradouro do Monte Agudo
Tips: Kiosk terrace with pergola shade and not a tourist in sight — the apartment quarter's own viewpoint, ~10 min from home. Good late-afternoon or pre-dinner leg-stretch.

Name: Casa Independente
Address: Largo do Intendente Pina Manique 45, 1100-285 Lisboa
Tips: Belle-epoque townhouse turned art space and courtyard bar on Largo do Intendente. Tiger Room concerts are a local institution — check the programme before going. 10 min walk from the apartment; evening drink territory, nothing like a tourist bar.

Name: Fabrica Braco de Prata
Address: Rua da Fabrica de Material de Guerra 1, 1950-128 Lisboa (Marvila)
Tips: Former ammunition factory turned book-lined culture complex — concerts, film, exhibitions across a warren of rooms. Friday-night live music if an evening ever needs an out-there option. Not on the plan; a Marvila add-on.
Family: Good — teens more than small kids

Name: Dois Corvos Taproom
Tips: The brewery that started Marvila's craft renaissance — 17 taps, tasting paddles, pub kitchen. Pairs with 8 Marvila two streets over. Weekend afternoons are when the district wakes up.

Name: Livraria do Simao
Tips: Four square metres wedged into a stair-arch — one customer at a time, the smallest bookshop in Lisbon. Sits ON the Day 3 Alfama descent route: 60 seconds of delight, zero detour.

Name: Museu da Marioneta
Tips: 5,000 puppets in a 17th-century convent. The African and Asian mask floor is the standout; check live-show times before committing. Off the tourist grid in Madragoa.
Family: Excellent — best small museum for kids in town

Name: Graca Bell-Tower Terrace (Igreja da Graca)
Cost Range: ~5 EUR (includes a drink at the esplanada)
Tips: The convent church's tower terrace — Portas do Sol views for a fraction of the crowd. Sunset-facing and almost always quiet. Pair with the Miradouro da Graca kiosk right below.

Name: Miradouro do Recolhimento
Tips: The secret terrace below the castle walls. Turn downhill off Rua da Graca and the view opens on your right. Rarely more than a handful of people.

Name: Largo do Contador-Mor
Tips: Sun-baked upper-Alfama square the tour groups never find — two minutes from the castle gate. Cards in the shade, cats on doorsteps. Natural pause on the Day 3 descent.

Name: Jardim Botto Machado
Tips: Small shaded garden beside the Panteao, missed by the Feira da Ladra crowds. The Day 3 recovery bench between the flea market and the Panteao.

Name: Jardim do Caracol da Penha
Tips: Brand-new hillside community park with a long metal slide and its own miradouro. 10 min from the apartment — the pre-dinner leg-stretch nobody else's guidebook has.
Family: Excellent — the slide is the draw

Name: Ascensor da Graca
